city_overview.hero_subtitle: From Morabadi to HEC, from Kanke to Dhurwa — every area is losing its mature green canopy, bird species, and clean air.

hotspots.name: HEC (Heavy Engineering Township)
hotspots.reason_for_cutting: Industrial township redevelopment, arterial corridor clearing & utility restructuring
hotspots.canopy_loss_status: Severe Loss: Historical green belt facing massive contiguous felling

hotspots.name: Dhurwa & Smart City Core
hotspots.reason_for_cutting: Ranchi Smart City institutional grids, commercial road corridors & administrative blocks
hotspots.primary_threat: Core Smart City sector development & Dhurwa roundabout widening
hotspots.official_record_ref: RMC / Smart City Master Plan Disclosures 2021-2024
hotspots.canopy_loss_status: Severe Loss: Hundreds of 50+ year old Sal & Banyan stands removed

hotspots.name: Morabadi (Tagore Hill & Grounds)
hotspots.reason_for_cutting: Tourism corridor expansion, stadium access routes, and commercial ground perimeter paving
hotspots.primary_threat: Tagore Hill approach road expansion & public ground commercialization
hotspots.aqi_monitoring_station: Morabadi Ambient Sensor / Nearest Albert Ekka Chowk
hotspots.official_record_ref: RMC Urban Forestry Division Annual Return 2023
hotspots.canopy_loss_status: Moderate Loss: Continuous cutting of avenue Mahua and Neem trees

hotspots.name: Kanke (Dam & Agricultural Belt)
hotspots.reason_for_cutting: Ring Road feeder 4-laning, residential encroachments into Kanke Dam catchment
hotspots.primary_threat: Real estate expansion along reservoir watershed & road expansion
hotspots.official_record_ref: Jharkhand Forest Dept / Kanke Range Gazette 2022-24
hotspots.canopy_loss_status: Moderate Loss: Encroaching onto historic waterfowl and raptor habitat

hotspots.name: Harmu (Housing Colony & Bypass)
hotspots.reason_for_cutting: Harmu Bypass multi-laning, riverfront concrete retaining wall construction, and commercial complexes
hotspots.primary_threat: Riverbank concreting destroyed natural riparian tree buffer
hotspots.canopy_loss_status: Severe Loss: Former green residential valley now consistently registers 'Very Poor' air

hotspots.name: Doranda (High Court Area & AG Colony)
hotspots.reason_for_cutting: Institutional road widening, utility shifting for government offices, and residential infill
hotspots.primary_threat: Old judicial campus renovation & arterial widening
hotspots.canopy_loss_status: Moderate Loss: Old British-era Tamarind and Banyan heritage trees cut down

hotspots.name: Hatia (Railway Terminal & Suburb)
hotspots.reason_for_cutting: Hatia Railway Station redevelopment, yard expansion & multi-modal transport access road
hotspots.primary_threat: Railway yard clearing & commercial logistics connectivity
hotspots.official_record_ref: South Eastern Railway Environmental Compliance Report 2024
hotspots.canopy_loss_status: Severe Loss: Dense station canopy largely replaced by concrete plazas

hotspots.name: Namkum (Industrial Belt & NH-33)
hotspots.reason_for_cutting: NH-33 four/six-laning, industrial warehouse parks, and railway line doubling
hotspots.primary_threat: Highway corridor expansion & logistics hub conversion
hotspots.canopy_loss_status: Moderate Loss: Sal copse forest patches fragmented along highway

hotspots.name: Piska More (Ratu Road Junction)
hotspots.reason_for_cutting: Ratu Road Elevated Flyover ramp touchdown, junction widening & commercial clearing
hotspots.primary_threat: Flyover construction and uncoordinated commercial bottleneck clearance
hotspots.canopy_loss_status: Severe Loss: Virtually 100% of large roadside canopy trees cut down

hotspots.name: Ratu Road (Flyover Corridor)
hotspots.reason_for_cutting: Construction of the 3.5 km elevated corridor from Zakir Hussain Park to Piska More
hotspots.primary_threat: Pillar construction, service lane expansion, utility trenching
hotspots.canopy_loss_status: Severe Loss: One of Ranchi's most polluted urban canyons following canopy loss

hotspots.name: Bariatu (RIMS Hospital Corridor)
hotspots.reason_for_cutting: RIMS road widening, new medical blocks, and utility expansion
hotspots.primary_threat: Emergency corridor widening & hospital campus development
hotspots.aqi_monitoring_station: Nearest Station: Morabadi / Albert Ekka Chowk
hotspots.canopy_loss_status: Moderate Loss: Shaded hospital avenue trees reduced to single sidewalk strip

hotspots.name: Kokar & Kantatoli Flyover Stretch
hotspots.reason_for_cutting: Kantatoli Flyover landing, Kokar industrial road widening & drainage overhaul
hotspots.official_record_ref: JUDCO Kantatoli Flyover DPR Review & Tree Compensation Audit
hotspots.canopy_loss_status: Severe Loss: Canopy loss caused dust concentration and chronic PM10 spikes

hotspots.name: Tupudana (Industrial & Khunti Link)
hotspots.reason_for_cutting: Industrial estate access road widening, heavy vehicle transit bypass
hotspots.primary_threat: Stone crusher traffic corridor and unpaved shoulder degradation
hotspots.canopy_loss_status: Moderate Loss: Continuous felling of scrub forest and roadside Mahua trees

hotspots.name: Birsa Munda Airport Road (Hinoo)
hotspots.reason_for_cutting: Airport expansion runway obstacle clearance, VIP road multi-laning & beautification
hotspots.primary_threat: Aviation height envelope clearance & road widening
hotspots.official_record_ref: AAI & Forest Department Tree Cutting Sanction 2021-2023
hotspots.canopy_loss_status: Severe Loss: Majestic 60-year-old Gulmohar and Eucalyptus avenues felled

hotspots.name: Ranchi Ring Road (Phases 3, 4, 7)
hotspots.reason_for_cutting: 85 km outer ring expressway construction, interchanges at Ormanjhi, Rampur, and Kathal More
hotspots.primary_threat: Massive perimeter forest clearing through rural tribal eco-belts
hotspots.official_record_ref: NHAI Regional Office Ranchi / Ring Road Environmental Audit 2024
hotspots.canopy_loss_status: Severe Loss: Largest single infrastructure contributor to district tree loss

aqi_trend_annual.notable_event: Pre-major flyover felling; mature urban canopy intact
COVID lockdown industrial slowdown & reduced vehicular dust
Kantatoli flyover clearing & Smart City phase 1 ground breaking
Ratu Road flyover tree cutting begins; airport road felling
Siramtoli-Mecon flyover construction + Ring Road phase 7 felling
Winter peak AQI exceeds 340 for 22 consecutive days
HEC / Dhurwa arterial survey notices & highest ever recorded dust days

area_insights.text: As trees fell in Harmu along the bypass and riverfront, annual average AQI rose by 72.5% (from 124 in 2019 to 214 in 2025).
As Smart City clearances began, Dhurwa AQI rose by 75.5% (from 98 in 2019 to 172 in 2025) — once Ranchi's cleanest urban forest refuge.
With zero tree canopy left along the flyover corridor, Ratu Road is now Ranchi's most toxic respiratory hotspot (annual average AQI 234).
Even Kanke, protected by the dam and agricultural university, experienced a 61.4% AQI surge as feeder road construction accelerated.

species_cards.iucn_status: Least Concern (Severely Threatened in Urban Canopy)
species_cards.where_seen_in_ranchi: HEC Sectors 2 & 3, Dhurwa Dam Link, Morabadi Tagore Hill, Doranda AG Colony
species_cards.why_trees_matter: Obligate hollow nester. Female seals herself inside deep tree cavities of 40+ year-old Peepal, Banyan, and Semal trees during nesting.
species_cards.consequence_if_cut: Immediate Local Reproductive Collapse: Will abandon area completely. Cannot breed in saplings for at least 40 to 50 years.

species_cards.iucn_status: State Bird of MP / Strict Canopy Migrant
species_cards.where_seen_in_ranchi: Dhurwa Forest Link, Morabadi, Kanke Dam Catchment, Rock Garden
species_cards.why_trees_matter: Feeds on aerial insects beneath dense shade of tall, continuous Sal, Mango, and Jamun canopies. Nests in deep shady tree forks.
species_cards.consequence_if_cut: Local Extinction: Requires contiguous canopy cover. Tree fragmentation removes insect micro-climate, causing permanent migration out of Ranchi city.

species_cards.iucn_status: Protected under Wildlife Protection Act (Schedule II)
species_cards.where_seen_in_ranchi: HEC, Morabadi, Harmu, Doranda, Bariatu, Kanke Dam
species_cards.why_trees_matter: Nests in natural cavities of old heritage trees and feeds on fruit, seeds, and blossoms of Gulmohar, Neem, and Shisham.
species_cards.consequence_if_cut: Will Leave: Loss of old hollow trunks forces parakeets out of residential areas into distant rural forest patches.

species_cards.where_seen_in_ranchi: Pahari Mandir foothills, HEC Old Foundry, Morabadi, Namkum outskirts
species_cards.why_trees_matter: Critical urban rodent predator; consumes 1,000+ rats per year per pair. Roosts in hollow Banyan and Peepal knot-holes.
species_cards.consequence_if_cut: Stop Breeding & Surge in Pests: With cavity trees gone, rodent populations multiply in human habitations.

species_cards.where_seen_in_ranchi: HEC Administrative Avenue, Kanke Road, Jagannathpur, Doranda
species_cards.why_trees_matter: Inhabits hollows of 30+ year old trees. Nocturnal feeder on beetles, moths, and crop pests.
species_cards.consequence_if_cut: Local Extinction: Unable to adapt to building crevices; felling of avenue trees directly destroys nesting pairs.

species_cards.where_seen_in_ranchi: Every sector in Ranchi with mature trees — Morabadi, HEC, Harmu, Bariatu
species_cards.why_trees_matter: Strict frugivore feeding on Ficus figs, Jamun, and Ber. Relies on dense canopy to parasitize crow nests for breeding.
species_cards.consequence_if_cut: Will Leave: Silence in Ranchi spring; canopy destruction drives koels out of urban neighbourhoods.

species_cards.where_seen_in_ranchi: Rock Garden, Kanke, Dhurwa, Morabadi, Hatia gardens
species_cards.why_trees_matter: Pollinates native flowering trees like Semal (Bombax ceiba), Palash (Butea monosperma), and Coral tree.
species_cards.consequence_if_cut: Severe Decline: Without mature nectar-bearing canopy trees, urban pollination chains break.

species_cards.where_seen_in_ranchi: HEC green avenues, Morabadi gardens, Kanke agricultural fields
species_cards.why_trees_matter: Stitches nests inside large living broadleaves of Mahua, Teak, and Mango. Cleans foliage of caterpillar pests.
species_cards.consequence_if_cut: Stop Breeding: Mechanical sapling pruning and loss of broadleaf mature foliage destroys nest sites.

species_cards.where_seen_in_ranchi: Dhurwa open fields, Kanke Dam, Ring Road border, Namkum
species_cards.why_trees_matter: Requires tall vantage perches on high mature branches to dive-bomb flying insects and protect passerine birds from raptors.
species_cards.consequence_if_cut: Will Leave: Loss of perch trees destroys hunting efficiency, causing insect pest outbreaks.

species_cards.iucn_status: Schedule II WPA / Keystone Seed Disperser
species_cards.where_seen_in_ranchi: HEC Sector 2 Colonial Trees, Doranda, Kanke Dam road, Tagore Hill
species_cards.why_trees_matter: Roosts exclusively in colonies of hundreds on giant 60+ year old Banyan and Peepal crowns. Ranchi's #1 forest seed disperser.
species_cards.consequence_if_cut: Complete Colony Collapse: Roost felling kills hundreds of bats and permanently halts native forest seed dispersion across 40 km radius.

species_cards.where_seen_in_ranchi: Kanke Dam catchment, Pithoria foothills, Ring Road Kathal More outer groves
species_cards.why_trees_matter: Roosts high in dense mature Sal, Mahua, and Banyan boughs at night to escape feral dogs and predators.
species_cards.consequence_if_cut: Local Extinction in Ranchi Suburbs: Ground nesting and roosting require undisturbed canopy cover; road felling leads to mortality by stray dogs and roadkill.

ecosystem_chain.headline: 1 Mature Tree = One Complete Living Ecosystem
ecosystem_chain.core_quote: You can plant a sapling in 1 day, but you cannot plant a 40-year-old nesting tree. It takes 20 years to become a home again.

links.title: 1 Mature Heritage Tree
links.description: A 40-year-old Sal, Banyan, or Peepal produces 118 kg oxygen/year, absorbs 24.5 kg CO2, and regulates subsoil water table.
links.status_when_cut: LOST: Cannot be replaced by saplings for 4 decades

links.title: 50+ Insect & Arthropod Species
links.description: Bark beetles, native honeybees, praying mantises, caterpillars, and wood-boring larvae thrive in foliage and trunk fissures.
links.status_when_cut: EXTIRPATED: Complete micro-habitat destruction in seconds

links.title: Birds, Bats & Small Fauna
links.description: Hornbills, owls, barbets, bats, and squirrels depend on hollows, fruits, and insects for daily food and breeding.
links.status_when_cut: DISPLACED / STARVED: Breeding failure and reproductive collapse

links.title: Natural Pest Control & Pollination
links.description: Birds and bats consume agricultural pests and mosquitoes, while pollinating native flora across Ranchi.
links.status_when_cut: BROKEN: Surge in mosquito-borne illness and pesticide necessity

links.title: Seed Dispersal & Wild Regeneration
links.description: Frugivores spread native seeds through droppings, allowing forest renewal without human intervention.
links.status_when_cut: CEASED: Forest regeneration stops; invasive weeds take over

links.title: Clean Air & Microclimate Cooling
links.description: Dense canopy cools ambient temperature by 3°C to 5°C and filters particulate dust (PM2.5 / PM10) from Ranchi air.
links.status_when_cut: COLLAPSED: Urban Heat Island effect & severe AQI spikes

child.label: Child (<12 years)
child.warning: Lungs are actively developing. Children inhale 50% more air per kg of body weight than adults, leading to early bronchial hyper-reactivity.

adult.label: Adult (18-59 years)
adult.warning: Chronic exposure accelerates atherosclerosis, reduces vital lung capacity, and causes recurring sinusitis and fatigue.

senior.label: Senior (60+ years)
senior.warning: Severe risk of acute cardiac events, stroke, COPD exacerbation, and secondary pneumonia during high AQI days.

hec_case_study.title: Spotlight Case Study: The HEC & Dhurwa Corridor Crisis
hec_case_study.subtitle: How the 10-Lane Road Threatens 7,000+ Heritage Trees — A Warning Bell for Ranchi's Final Green Refuge
key_takeaways: The Vivekananda School More to Naya Sarai road stretch features one of Ranchi's densest contiguous Sal, Banyan, and Peepal avenues.
The current SHAJ-111047-1 60-meter right-of-way design threatens over 7,000 trees with zero public consultation.
Lessons from Ratu Road and Kantatoli prove that compensatory afforestation fails to replace mature urban canopy, turning shaded corridors into severe heat islands.
hec_case_study.citizen_mitigation_proposal: Adopt a split-carriageway design preserving median heritage trees, reducing paved ROW from 60m to 35m, saving 82% of mature trees.
